14_marg901: AND KING DAVID WAS OLD. Does it not seem to thee, if thou follow the letter that kills, to be a fiction or a farce of Athens? A cold old man is wrapped in clothes and is not warmed except by the embrace of a young girl. Bethsabee was still living, Abigail survived, and the other wives and concubines. All are rejected as if cold, and the aged man grows warm in the embraces of one alone. Abraham was much older than David, and yet while Sara lived he did not seek another wife. Isaac had twice David's years, and with Rebecca, now an old woman, he never grew cold. I say nothing of the earlier men before the flood, who after five hundred years, with limbs not merely aged but almost decayed, never sought girlish embraces. Moses, the leader of the people of Israel, had a hundred and twenty years, and did not change Sephora. Who then is this Sunamitess, wife and virgin, so fervent that she could warm the cold, so holy that she did not provoke the warm to lust? Let Solomon expound his father's delights, and the peaceable one the embraces of the warrior: "Get wisdom, get understanding; forsake her not, and she shall keep thee. Love her, and she shall preserve thee." Almost all the powers of the body are changed in old men, and while wisdom alone increases, the rest decrease: fasts, sleeping on the ground, running here and there, receiving of strangers, defence of the poor, urgency of prayers, visiting the sick, labour of the hands from which alms are supplied; and all things that are exercised through the body become less when the body is broken. Nor do I say this as though in the young, and those of still firmer age, who by labour and most ardent study, and also by holiness of life and frequency of prayer, have attained knowledge, wisdom grows cold, which in very many old men withers with age; but that youth sustains many wars of the body, and amid the incentives of vices and the ticklings of the flesh is smothered like fire in green wood and cannot fill out its own brightness. But the old age of those who have furnished their youth with honest acts and have meditated in the law of the Lord day and night becomes more learned with age, wiser with the passage of time, and reaps the sweetest fruits of its old studies. And the very name Abisag indicates the more ample wisdom of old men. For it is interpreted 'my father superfluous', that is, abounding, or 'roaring of my father'. The word 'superfluous' is ambiguous, but here it signifies that wisdom is more ample and overflowing in old men; elsewhere 'superfluous' is put as if 'not necessary'. And Abisag is properly called 'roaring' too, because the wave of the sea resounds, and, so to speak, a roar is heard coming from the deep. By which it is shown that the thunder of the divine word abides in old men most abundantly and beyond the human voice. And Sunamitess is called 'scarlet', to signify that wisdom is warm and glows with divine reading. Which, though it points to the sacrament of the Lord's blood, also shows the fervour of wisdom. Whence that midwife in Genesis binds a scarlet thread on the hand of Phares, who, from his having divided the wall that before separated the two peoples, obtained the name of divider, that is, Phares. And Rahab the harlot, in the type of the Church, hung up the cord containing the mystery of blood, that when Jericho perished her house might be saved. Whence it is said of the saints: "These are they that came of the heat of the house of Rechab," and elsewhere: "I am come to cast fire on the earth" etc., which, kindled in the hearts of the disciples, compelled them to say: "Was not our heart burning?"
14_marg902: AND WHEN HE WAS COVERED etc. David suffered excessive cold, either because he was born of elderly parents, or because he had shed much blood in battle, or rather because, from the time he saw the angel slaying the people, he wasted away with vehement dread; whence he remained in the affliction of cold until death.

14_marg903: He signifies the Jewish people, which seems to be the elder son, because it received the law first, and, spurning the gentile people, which was called later by the grace of God, thought that it alone would reign with the Lord. 14_marg904: It is interpreted 'daughter of the oath'. And it signifies the ancient Church that was under the law, of whose stock the true Solomon was promised to be born. Nathan is interpreted 'gift', and figures the old prophecy.
14_marg905: [The mule of] David: some say [it signifies] the Church, others the Synagogue, on account of its unfruitfulness.
14_marg906: David instructs Solomon concerning the just recompense of those who were a comfort to him, or who unjustly harmed him, whom he himself patiently bore. And the prophecy indicates what must be done to the wicked or the good in the future, which the true Solomon will fulfil. Meanwhile, however, the patience of God often allows the good to be afflicted, the reprobate to enjoy delights.
14_marg907: Solomon bears the figure of Christ. For he builds the temple, as Christ the Church. He had peace according to his name, as the Lord himself too is called the king of peace, making peace to those far off and peace to those near. And there is no doubt that in wisdom and riches and glory he bore the type of the Saviour.
14_marg908: THEN BETHSABEE CAME TO SPEAK FOR ADONIAS. Adonias, through the intervention of Bethsabee, who is interpreted 'daughter of fulness', longed to corrupt Abisag the Sunamitess, because the Jewish people, through the observance of the law with which it was sated, wished to violate the spiritual understanding, or the Church, which is an incorrupt virgin joined to our David; and because it did not deserve her fellowship, it incurred the death it deserved. Nor did Bethsabee, interceding with Solomon for Adonias, profit him anything, nor the law which the Jews think to be their helper with God.
14_marg909: Abiathar, expelled from the priesthood yet not killed, signifies the Jews, whose priesthood, though abolished, they themselves have not been destroyed, for the sake of those of them who will believe at the end of the world.
14_marg910: Joab, who, fleeing to the altar, was killed there at Solomon's command, signifies the masters of perverse doctrine, who, because they destroy churchmen by plots, as Joab [did] Abner and Amasa, will be driven from the altar of faith and punished with everlasting death. But to David and his seed be peace for ever; that is, the enemies of Christ being abolished, the throne of David, that is, the Church, enjoying eternal peace, will remain for ever.
14_marg911: AND GO NOT OUT. The true Solomon commands us who dwell in Jerusalem never to go out. And if those before subject to us flee from us, let us not therefore go out to follow the footsteps of the fugitives, lest while we wish to save those fleeing we ourselves perish; but rather let the dead bury the dead, and while we may, let us pluck out and cut off from us the eye, hand or foot that scandalizes.
14_marg912: FOR HE TOOK HIS DAUGHTER etc. The daughter of Pharao, whom Solomon joined to himself in marriage, signified 'the Church from the gentiles'.
14_marg913: The people sacrificed chiefly on the mountains, either to God or to demons.
14_marg914: In Gabaon was the greatest high place, where was the tabernacle which Moses made, and the brazen altar, upon which Solomon, offering a thousand victims, deserved the divine oracle.

14_marg916: THEN THERE CAME TWO WOMEN. GREGORY. After the Lord illumines the darkness of our error with the light of his knowledge, he soon tests [us], visiting [us] with the sting of temptation; because by approaching he advances our hearts to virtues, and by withdrawing he allows them to be shaken by temptation. For if after the gifts of virtues it is shaken by no temptation, the mind glories that it has this of itself. That it may have the gifts of firmness, then, and acknowledge its infirmity, it is lifted to the heights by the approach of grace, and by the withdrawal it is proved what it is of itself. Whence Solomon, after receiving wisdom from God, is struck by the dispute of the harlots. Because often, when the regard of the inward bounty illumines our mind with the virtues granted, slippery thoughts soon trouble it, so that she who, lifted up, exults in the immense gift, may also, struck by temptation, find out what she is. So Elias too, visited from above, opened the heavens by his word, and suddenly, proved weak, fleeing through the deserts, dreaded one woman. So Paul, penetrating even to the third heaven, beholds the secrets of paradise, and returning to himself labours against the war of the flesh. He bears another law in his members, by whose rebellion in him he grieves that the law of the spirit is wearied. After the giving of the gift, then, God tests man, because he both lifts him up by bestowing the gift and, withdrawing it a little, shows him to himself. This we suffer so that we may be reformed to the substance of the promised incorruption.
14_marg917: Some judge that this is to be understood of the Synagogue and the Church, and referred to that time when, after the cross and resurrection, the true Solomon, that is, the peaceable one, began to reign both among the Jews and among the gentiles. For Osee took a wife of fornications, then an adulteress. For Christ came for this, to give harlots in marriage and to make of two flocks one fold. These are the two rods which are joined in Ezechiel, and of which it is said by Zacharias: "And I took unto me two rods, one I called Beauty, and the other I called a Cord." That woman too in the gospel who washed the feet of Jesus with tears, wiped them with her hair, and to whom all sins were forgiven, signifies the Church gathered from the gentiles. Yet the Church "has no spot or wrinkle"; nor do we say that she remained a harlot, but that she had been, according to what is said: 'When Jesus was in the house of Simon the leper', not one who was then a leper but who had been before. Note too what the Church says against the Synagogue: I AND THIS WOMAN DWELT IN ONE HOUSE etc., because after the resurrection of the Saviour one [Church] was gathered from both peoples. And elegantly he added: I WAS DELIVERED OF A CHILD WITH HER IN THE CHAMBER. For the Church from the gentiles, which did not have the law and the prophets, gave birth in the house of the Synagogue, and did not go out of the chamber but went in. Whence: "The king hath brought me into his chamber," and: "I will bring thee into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that bore me."
14_marg918: If thou consider Pilate washing his hands and saying: "I am innocent of the blood of this just man," and the centurion confessing: "Indeed this was the Son of God," and those who before the passion desired through Philip to see the Lord, thou wilt not doubt that the first to give birth was the Church, and that afterwards was born the people of the Jews, for whom the Lord prayed: "Father, forgive them" etc., and: "There believed in one day three thousand," and another five thousand.
14_marg919: GREGORY. By the nursing mothers is signified the order of teachers, by their sons the person of the disciples. For masters watchful in knowledge but asleep in life, while they neglect to do what they say, kill through the sleep of torpor their hearers, whom they nourish through the vigils of preaching, and by neglect overlay those whom they seemed to feed with the milk of words. Whence, while they live reprehensibly and cannot have disciples of praiseworthy life, they try to draw others' disciples to themselves, that, by showing that they have good followers, they may excuse before the judgments of men the evils they do, and cover their deadly negligence by the life of their subjects. Whence the woman who killed her own son sought another's; but the sword of Solomon found the true mother, because the wrath of the judge at the last examination will show for whom the fruit lives or perishes. And note that the living son is first ordered to be divided, that afterwards he may be given back to the mother alone; because in this life the life of the disciple is allowed to be as it were shared, while from it one is permitted to have merit with God, another praise with men. But the false mother did not fear that he whom she had not borne should be killed, because arrogant masters, ignorant of charity, if they cannot obtain the fullest name of praise from others' disciples, cruelly persecute their life. For, kindled with envy, they do not wish those to live for others whom they see they cannot possess. Whence: LET IT BE NEITHER MINE NOR THINE. For those whom they do not see serving them for temporal glory, they begrudge to live for others through the truth. But the true mother is anxious that her son at least be with a stranger and live, because truthful masters allow that others have the praise of mastership from their disciples, provided these do not lose integrity of life. By which bowels of pity this same true mother is recognized, because mastership is wholly approved in the examination of charity. She alone deserved to receive the whole who as it were gave up the whole; because faithful superiors, since from good disciples they not only do not begrudge others praise but even pray for the profit of their advancement, themselves receive their sons whole and living, when at the last judgment they obtain perfect recompense from their life.

The two women, in one of whom love burned, in the other pretence crept in, figure the Church and the Synagogue, or heretical depravity, each of which [the latter] both kills her own by wicked nursing and entices others until she destroys them. Between the two women the Lord, while he decides what is just by the spirit of his mouth, restores to each what is due.

14_marg934: Hyssop, a lowly herb clinging to the rock, signifies the humility of Christ, who treated from the cedar to the hyssop, because he came down from the excellence of heavenly glory to the humility of the flesh. By the cedar too the pride of the wicked is designated. Whence: "The voice of the Lord breaketh the cedars." From the cedar to the hyssop, then, Christ treats, because he judges the hearts of the proud and of the humble. He also treated about wood [super lignis] when he hung on the cross. For then he bowed the cedar, that is, the arrogance of the world, down to the humility of the hyssop, that is, to the foolishness of the cross: "For the word of the cross, to them indeed that perish, is foolishness; but to them that are saved, it is the power of God." And a little after: "For seeing that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of our preaching to save them that believe."
14_marg935: AND HE DISCOURSED etc. RABANUS. For all things are naked and open to Christ, nor is there any creature invisible in his sight. He knows the thoughts of men and tells the multitude of the stars; to him the abyss lies open, and hell is not hidden before him. And he discourses when he sets before us the reason of each thing and makes manifest in the Scriptures the sacraments hidden from ages and generations, that we may consider the beatitude of the angels, the profit of men, the cunning of the demons, and, rejecting what is evil, follow what is good.
14_interl1379: Hence Isaias: And all nations shall flow unto it, and many people shall go and say: "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord"
14_marg936: TO BUILD A HOUSE. BEDE. The house which Solomon built was a figure of the Church, which from the first elect to the last is daily built by the grace of the peaceable king, that is, Christ; which partly is a pilgrim from him on earth, partly, after its pilgrimage, already reigns with him in heaven, where after the last judgment it will reign whole. To it belong the angels, likeness to whom is promised us in the future. Whence: "They are equal to the angels, and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection." To it belongs Christ himself also. Whence: "Destroy this temple, and in three [days] I will raise it up." "But he spoke of the temple of his body." And of us the Apostle says: "Know you not that you are the temple of God" etc. If, then, he was made a temple according to the flesh, and we are made the temple of God by the indwelling Spirit, it is certain that that temple was a figure of all of us and of the Lord himself, that is, of the members and the head: but of him as the chief cornerstone, elect, precious, laid in the foundation; of us as living stones built up upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, that is, Christ. This will appear better when the order of the building of the temple itself is considered, so that in some things the figure pertains to him himself, in some to all the elect, in some it shows the unspoiled happiness of the angels in heaven, in some the help of the angels bestowed on men, in some the contests of men rewarded with the angels.
14_marg937: This spiritual house the tabernacle made in the desert also signifies. But [there is a difference], because that house [was made] on the journey by which they were coming to the land of promise, this was built in the land itself and in the city of Jerusalem; that, so that, carried often from place to place by the ministry of the Levites, it might at length be brought into the land of the promised inheritance; this, so that, set up at once in the homeland itself and in the royal city, it might stand ever on an inviolable foundation until it fulfilled the office of heavenly figures laid upon it. In that can be figured the labour and exile of the present Church, in this the future rest and beatitude. Or, because that was made by the children of Israel alone, this by proselytes also and gentiles, in that can be expressed principally the fathers of the old Testament and the ancient people of God,
14_marg938: in this the Church gathered from the gentiles. Although each building, discussed more closely, shows in manifold figures both the daily labours of the present Church and the eternal rewards in the future, and the joys of the heavenly kingdom, and also the election of the primitive Church and the salvation of all nations in Christ.
14_marg939: GIVE ORDERS THEREFORE THAT THEY CUT ME DOWN CEDAR TREES OUT OF LIBANUS etc. The servants of Hiram cutting cedars for Solomon from Libanus are the chosen teachers from the gentiles, who, by correcting them, cut down from the pomp of pride those who rejoice in the things and glory of the world, and transfer them to the service of Christ; with whom the servants of Solomon press on in the said work, because the first teachers from the gentiles needed to be instructed by the teaching of the apostles, who learned from the Lord, lest, if they began to teach without masters, they should be masters of error. For Solomon wished the servants of Hiram to cut the wood for this reason, because in cutting they were more skilled than his servants. He also wished his own to be present, to show the measures to the cutters. The apostles too knew the word of the gospel more surely from him himself, but the gentiles, converted from error to the truth of the gospel, knew the errors of the gentiles better, and therefore fought them more skilfully.
14_marg940: BEDE. We must speak first of the workmen of the temple, who they were and whence, and of the material itself. "For all these things happened to them in figure, and they are written for us." Solomon, about to build a house to the Lord, sought help from Hiram king of Tyre, who was ever a friend of David, and had already begun to have peace with Solomon himself; and he found him ready in all things, so that he gave him craftsmen and timber and gold as he needed. And Solomon repaid every year very many measures of wheat and oil. Solomon, that is, 'peaceable', both by name and by the most tranquil state of his kingdom signifies Christ, of whom it is said: "His empire shall be multiplied, and there shall be no end of peace." And Hiram, who is interpreted 'living on high', [signifies] gentiles glorious in life and faith. Or, because he was a king and helped Solomon with royal power in the building of the temple, he signifies the lords of the world converted to the faith, by whose aid the Church is increased and is raised up by princely decrees against heretics and schismatics [and] pagans. Solomon, then, asks help from Hiram in the work of the temple, because the Lord, coming in the flesh and wishing to build the Church, chose helpers not from the Jews only but also from the gentiles. For from both peoples he took ministers of the word. Hiram sent Solomon cedar wood cut from Libanus, and fir, to be set in the house of the Lord, because the converted gentile world sent to the Lord men famous in the world, but cast down and humbled from the mountain of pride by the axe of rebuke, who, instructed to the rule of gospel truth, were placed in the building of the Church each according to his merit or time. He also sent craftsmen, that is, philosophers converted to true wisdom, who were set over the peoples to be ruled for the sake of learning; such was in the times of the apostles Dionysius the Areopagite, and Cyprian, a most learned teacher and most valiant martyr. He sent also gold, namely men famous for wisdom and talent, in return for whom he awaits the gifts of heavenly grace: the wheat, namely, of God, the oil of charity, of the anointing and illumination of the Holy Spirit.
14_marg941: SO HIRAM GAVE SOLOMON etc. Tyre, whence king Hiram [came], is an island given to trade, where there were excellent workers of timber, who gave precious timber receiving provisions. For they live not by tilling the land but by trading. There is mount Libanus, from whose timber the house of the Lord was made. Whence [the temple] too is called Libanus, there: "Open thy gates, O Libanus."
14_interl1380: because it was enjoined on each what he should do
14_marg942: AND KING SOLOMON CHOSE WORKMEN OUT OF ALL ISRAEL etc. Not in vain did he choose workmen out of all Israel, because those who build the house of God by example and word are not to be chosen from the one stock of Aaron the priest, but sought from the whole Church, and promoted without respect of persons. When they are ordained to instruct the unbelievers and call them into the college of the Church, vigorous and chosen men are sent as it were to cut the materials of the temple in Libanus. The thirty thousand cutters signify those who are perfect in the faith of the Trinity, which befits teachers most of all. But because the thirty thousand were so ordered that ten [thousand] pressed on the work each month, the sacrament of the ten is rather to be opened. Ten thousand are sent from Israel to cut timber for the work of the house of the Lord, for those who are ordained to the instruction of the ignorant must keep the ten precepts of the law in all things and show them to their hearers to be kept. The rewards to come in heaven also are figured by the denarius, which they themselves must hope for and make known to their hearers as to be hoped for. And the three months, whose interval was laid on the individual cutters of timber, typically announce the perfection of the three gospel virtues: almsgiving, prayer and fasting. For by almsgiving are comprehended all things which we work kindly toward the brethren to fulfil the love of neighbour; by prayer all things by which through inward compunction we are joined to our creator; by fasting all things by which we keep ourselves from the contagion of vices and the enticements of the world, that with free mind and chaste body we may always be able to cleave to the love of God and neighbour. These are the three months of the workmen of the temple; for because a month is completed by the fulness of the days of the lunar circle, by it is rightly shown the fulness of virtue, in which the mind of the faithful is looked upon by the Lord with daily illumination, as the moon by the sun.
14_marg943: These workmen were proselytes, their masters from the Jews, because he did not make anyone of Israel to serve.
14_interl1381: the month of cutting [is] almsgiving, by which we profit our neighbours; the two, prayer and fasting
14_marg944: Adoniram: 'my Lord on high'. This is Christ, who is set over the workmen of the temple, to order in which months each should go out to work and in which return to care for his own house; when he more familiarly informs the minds of preachers, that they may discern when they ought to build the Church by preaching, or by performing other offices of piety, and when to return to examine their conscience, as if to inspect their own house, that by prayers and fasts it may be worthy of the heavenly inspector and visitor.
14_marg945: AND SOLOMON HAD SEVENTY THOUSAND etc. Nor should it be passed over that the seventy and eighty thousand burden-bearers and stonecutters, with their overseers, were not Israelites, but proselytes, that is, strangers who dwelt among them. Whence in Paralipomenon: "Solomon numbered all the proselytes, and there were found a hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred. And he made seventy thousand of them to carry burdens on their shoulders" etc. Now they were called proselytes in Greek who passed from other nations into the fellowship of the people of God, having received circumcision. The workmen of the house of the Lord, then, were of Israel, and of the proselytes, and of the gentiles: of Israel the thirty thousand who were sent to cut cedars from Libanus; of the proselytes these stonecutters; of the gentiles Hiram and his servants, who cut timber with the servants of Solomon. Every kind of men, then, through whom the Church was to be built, went before in the building of the temple. For Jews, proselytes and gentiles converted to the truth build the one Church of Christ by right living and teaching.
14_marg946: Seventy thousand and eighty thousand workmen: seventy, namely, on account of the sabbath rest of souls, for the seventh day is consecrated to the sabbath, that is, to rest; eighty on account of the hope of resurrection, which went before in the Lord on the eighth day, that is, after the sabbath, and in us is hoped for on the eighth day and in the eighth age to come.
14_marg947: BEDE. Latomi are cutters of stones, and signify the same as the cutters of timber, that is, preachers, who work the minds of the ignorant with the chisel of the word of God, and change them from their native crookedness and deformity, and, regularly instructed, fit them to the unity of the faithful, that is, to the building of the house of God. Timber and stones are cut on the mountain and carried to the mountain of the house of God, because we are all born on the mountain of pride, who draw our origin from the sin of Adam, who sinned proudly. But we are hewn out of the mountain of pride by being catechized and receiving the sacraments of faith, and are carried to the mountain of the house of the Lord, because, rescued from the power of darkness, we come to the citadel of virtues, which is in the unity of the Church.
14_marg948: And note that some cut stones on the mountain, some carried burdens. For the gifts of the spirit are diverse, and some have greater constancy in teaching and reproving the insolent; some are gentler, for consoling the fainthearted; some, endowed with both virtues, come together for the work of the house of the Lord. Whence: "Rebuke the unquiet, comfort the feebleminded" etc.
14_marg949: The overseers are the authors of sacred Scripture, by whose mastery we are instructed to teach the ignorant, to rebuke the contemptuous, and to bear one another's burdens.
14_marg950: On account of the faith of the Trinity, which the holy words preach. That in Paralipomenon three thousand six hundred are written looks to their perfection. For the six, in which the adornment of the world was completed, signifies perfect good works; and because holy Scripture teaches that the works of justice are to be had with the faith of truth, the overseers of the works of the temple were rightly three thousand six hundred.
14_marg951: AND THE KING COMMANDED THAT THEY SHOULD BRING etc. To build the house of the Lord, first timber and stones are cut from the mountain, because those whom we seek to instruct in the faith we must first teach to renounce the devil and the transgression in which they were born. Then great and precious stones are to be sought and laid in the foundation, so that, the former conversation being renounced, we may look into their life and conduct in all things, and set before our hearers for imitation those whom we know to cleave specially to the Lord through the virtue of humility, and whom we see, squared by stability of mind, to endure unmoved against all onsets of temptations, great and precious in fame and merit.
14_marg952: Namely men eminent in action and holiness, who cleave more familiarly to Christ, so that the more firmly they hope in him, the more strongly they may be able to direct the life of others, which is to bear the breadth of the wall. These are the prophets [and] apostles, who received the word and sacraments of truth visibly or invisibly from the very wisdom of God. Whence: "Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets."
14_marg953: GREAT STONES, COSTLY STONES. Or the great, precious, squared stones are the first masters, who heard the word of salvation from the Lord himself; and the rows of stones or timbers laid above are the following priests or teachers, by whose preaching the Church grows and is adorned with virtues.
14_marg954: BEDE. RABANUS. And of what colour the stones were, David shows in Paralipomenon, saying to Solomon: 'I have prepared every precious stone and Parian marble in great abundance'. He calls Parian marble white, such as the island of Paros produces. Whence the Poet: "Olearos and snowy Paros" etc. Whence Josephus: "He raised the temple up to the vault, built of white stone." The white marble of which the house of the elect is built signifies clean action and a conscience chastened from every blemish of corruption. Whence: "Let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of the flesh and of the spirit, perfecting sanctification in the fear of God."
14_marg955: The foundation is Christ; whence: "Other foundation no man can lay, but that which is laid, which is Christ Jesus." Who is rightly called the foundation of the house of God, because, as Peter says: "There is no other name under heaven given to men, whereby we must be saved." On him are brought great and precious stones, that is, all the perfect, who faithfully cleave to him and bravely bear the necessities of the brethren, and are bent from their rectitude by no adversity, nor even by death; whom the Church receives not only from Judea but also from the gentiles. Whence it is added: which the masons of Solomon hewed etc.
14_interl1383: who prepare or lay on the cement
14_marg956: Because the teachers of the Church were from both peoples, and so lofty that they were the teachers even of those lofty teachers themselves, and as it were squaring them prepared them for raising the building of the house of the Lord. For not only Jeremias, Isaias and the other prophets of the circumcision, but also Job with his sons, who were of the gentiles, minister the greatest pattern of life and patience [and] the greatest proclamations of saving doctrine to the teachers who follow, that, superfluous words, deeds and thoughts being cast away, they may become worthy to bear the burden of the Church.
14_marg957: RABANUS. BEDE. Byblos is a city of Phenicia, of which Ezechiel [says]: "The ancients of Gebal, and the wise men thereof" etc. For which in the Hebrew is had Goel or Gebal, which is interpreted 'defining' or 'discriminating'. For those who prepare the hearts of men for the spiritual building which the soul constructs out of virtues are then able to have or teach their hearers faith and works of justice, if they have first, taught by the sacred pages, learned by a certain definition of truth what faith is to be held, by what path of virtues one must go. In vain does he usurp the office of teacher who does not know the discernment of faith. Nor does he build a sanctuary for the Lord but a ruin for himself who presumes to teach what he himself has not learned.
14_marg958: After the foundation composed of such [stones], the house is to be built with timber and stones prepared and set in order, which have been drawn from their place or root; because after the first rudiments of faith, after the foundations of humility laid in us after the example of lofty men, the wall of good works is to be added on high, and, as it were with rows of stones laid one on another, we must advance from virtue to virtue.
